newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL stocks end weaker after choppy session.
newsitem.headline: KL stocks end weaker after choppy session.

text.p: Gains in Kuala Lumpur blue chips evaporated in the second half of the day as investors grabbed profits after the market's bullish streak.
Caution in front of Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's testimony in Congress on Wednesday may have also provided an excuse for the backtracking, dealers said.

After scoring a new session peak at 1,278.94, the Composite Index of key 100 stocks sank 6.20 points to 1,265.37. The small-cap Second Board slipped 3.89 points to 640.03 after failing to hold a morning gain.
"I think people are resting up," said Ami Moris, a vice president in dealing at CapitalCorp. "They're squaring off positions ahead of the month-end. They're just wisely taking profits."
Turnover remained robust, at over 916 million shares compared with 812 million on Tuesday. Losers outpaced gainers by 442 to 214.

"There's no more buyers," said William Chan, institutional dealer at Seagroatt & Campbell, noting the strong volumes in recent past sessions. "Those who wanted to buy have bought. You're seeing a shakeout."
